chunks: Consider the water that you drink.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of water in Surah Al-Waqi'ah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to emphasize Tawhid (monotheism) by contrasting human dependence on a natural element with the ultimate sovereignty of Allah, who alone controls its distribution. It serves as a reminder of divine providence (Rizq) and encourages gratitude (Shukr) for sustenance that is not earned by human effort but granted by God's will.
